title.narrative: Provision of cash assistance for shelter and NFIs to vulnerable households affected by floods in Lao Cai Province

description.narrative: The recent typhoon, followed by floods and landslides, severely impacted northern and mountainous provinces of Viet Nam, causing widespread destruction and compounding pre-existing vulnerabilities. The disaster led to more than 237,000 homes damaged, 73,248 of which were submerged in floodwaters. The aftermath of Typhoon Yagi also resulted in widespread displacement, as many individuals were forced to evacuate or leave their homes due to severe damage. This sudden displacement is putting immense pressure on the local government and communities to accommodate large numbers of people and provide essential services, whose duration of need remains uncertain. In under-resourced provinces, the situation is even more challenging, as limited resources and infrastructure make it difficult to manage the growing demand for temporary housing and necessities. IOM will support temporarily displaced populations affected by Typhoon Yagi by providing cash for shelter repairs and cash grants for essential non-food items (NFIs). The assistance will target two districts in Lao Cai province, reaching 7,020 people including 1,805 households (6,220 people) for essential items and 200 households (800 people) for shelter repairs, focusing on homes with minor damage (30 per cent or less) to enable a return within three months while other complementary projects support reconstruction of destroyed homes, which will require longer than three months.Emergency shelter and NFI assistance will focus on (i) repairing damaged houses through conditional cash, prioritizing overcrowded households in evacuation shelters or those hosted by other families, and (ii) providing NFIs through cash grants to help families stay or return to safe homes with privacy and dignity, especially for women and girls, while easing pressure on national and local emergency response systems.This CERF action responds to the needs identified by the Government of Viet Nam’s the Vietnam Disaster Management Authority, and the Shelter and NFIs sector in the Typhoon Yagi and Floods Joint Response Plan, namely the urgent need to repair damaged homes and provide NFIs to ensure that affected populations have safe and secure living conditions through cash-based interventions.
